cases.reason: X is tighter and comes with a ready-made blanked self-quiz version and answer key, whereas Y runs to several pages with extra content (Hereward, sources, historian questions) that defeats the one-page purpose.

Y gives a timed, teachable plan for every lesson at a realistic pace, while X has stronger spaced retrieval and checks but crams 15-minute checks into lessons that also introduce new content (e.g. lists plus a practical check in L10) and includes stray internal references.
X follows a clear predict-modify-make progression with test tables, staged hints and full worked solutions, whereas Y jumps quickly to writing from scratch and has few test cases or hints.

Both are strong, but Y's single printed sheet with consistent timings and a named hand-in gives clearer evidence of what was done, while X's board outline timings (55 min, 5 vs 2 min exit ticket) do not match its own table.
